guides.title: Mac screenshot guides | EasyShoot
guides.description: Short, practical guides for screenshots on Mac: shortcuts, cropping, backgrounds, blurring private details, arrows and steps, and text on images.
guides.intro: Short answers to the things people ask most about screenshots on a Mac, with the exact keys to press.

compare.title: EasyShoot compared with other Mac screenshot apps
compare.description: How EasyShoot compares with CleanShot X, Shottr, Snagit and the screenshot tool built into macOS, with honest notes on when each one fits better.
compare.intro: Looking for a different screenshot app for your Mac? Here is how EasyShoot lines up with the tools people usually compare it with, including where another tool is the better pick.

blur-screenshot-mac.title: How to blur or pixelate part of a screenshot on Mac | EasyShoot
blur-screenshot-mac.description: Hide emails, card numbers and faces in a screenshot on your Mac before you share it. Pixelate or blur any area in seconds with EasyShoot.
blur-screenshot-mac.h1: How to blur part of a screenshot on a Mac
blur-screenshot-mac.intro: Before you share a screenshot, hide what isn't yours to share: an email address, a card number, a name or a face. EasyShoot pixelates or blurs any area you drag over, and nothing leaves your Mac while you do it.

steps.name: Capture or open the image
steps.text: Take a screenshot with EasyShoot, or copy an image and choose Open from Clipboard.

steps.name: Choose Pixelate
steps.text: Press B, or click the Pixelate tool. In the Style tab, pick Pixels or Blur and set the Strength.

steps.name: Drag over the private part
steps.text: Drag a box over the text or face. Draw more boxes for other details.

steps.name: Copy or save
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-C to copy, or Command-S to save. The pixelated area is part of the exported image.

sections.html: Cover just the detail that is private. A screenshot with one small hidden area still explains itself; one that is half blurred doesn't.
EasyShoot has no account and no cloud. Your screenshot stays on your Mac while you edit it, and only goes where you copy or save it.

faq.q: Can macOS blur part of a screenshot on its own?
faq.a: Apple's Markup guide lists shapes, text, highlight, sketch, loupe and crop, but not a blur or pixelate tool, so people usually use an app for this.

faq.q: Is pixelation or blur reversible?
faq.a: The exported image only contains the pixelated or blurred area, not the original detail.

faq.q: Can I pixelate after adding arrows and steps?
faq.a: Yes. Every mark stays editable until you export, in any order.

annotate-screenshot-mac.title: Add arrows, text and steps to a Mac screenshot | EasyShoot
annotate-screenshot-mac.description: Mark up screenshots on your Mac with arrows, boxes, text and numbered steps, one key per tool. A quick guide with EasyShoot.
annotate-screenshot-mac.h1: How to add arrows and numbered steps to a screenshot on a Mac
annotate-screenshot-mac.intro: A good screenshot points at one thing and says what to do. EasyShoot gives every markup tool a single key, so you can box, number and point without reaching for the mouse.

steps.name: Capture the screen
steps.text: Press Option-Shift-Command-4 and drag over an area. A thumbnail appears in the corner of the screen: double-click it to open the capture in the editor. To open the editor right away without the thumbnail, turn on Open editor after capture in Settings › General.

steps.name: Box the important part
steps.text: Press R and drag a rectangle around it, leaving a little space so the line doesn't cross text.

steps.name: Number the steps
steps.text: Press N and click beside each thing in order. The numbers count themselves: 1, 2, 3.

steps.name: Point and explain
steps.text: Press A to draw an arrow, or T to add a short note.

steps.name: Share
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-C to copy and paste it straight into Messages, Slack or Mail.

sections.html:
ToolKey
ArrowA
LineL
RectangleR
DiamondD
EllipseO
TextT
Numbered stepN
PenP
PixelateB
CropC

• Lines and shapes: solid, dashed or dotted strokes, from thin to bold.
  • Rectangle, Diamond and Ellipse: a fill and an outline you can hide, rounded corners from sharp to round, a shadow and any angle.
  • Arrows: a standard or swept head; drag the middle handle to bend one.
  • Numbered steps: no background, their own colour or a light fill.
  • Several at once: Command-A, Shift-click or drag a box over empty canvas, then move, restyle or delete them together.

• Use three or four marks at most: one box, a couple of numbers, one arrow.
  • Put numbers beside what they mark, not on top of text.
  • Change colour, stroke width and opacity for any mark in the Style tab.

faq.q: Can I edit a mark after drawing it?
faq.a: Yes. Every mark stays editable until you export the image.

faq.q: Can I use my own font for text?
faq.a: Yes. Text can use any font installed on your Mac.

faq.q: Can I save my favourite style?
faq.a: Yes. Save a background, mark style and export format as a preset, and make it the default.

arabic-text-screenshot-mac.title: How to write Arabic text on a screenshot on Mac | EasyShoot
arabic-text-screenshot-mac.description: Add Arabic or Hebrew text to screenshots on your Mac with correct right-to-left direction and letter shaping, in any font. A guide with EasyShoot.
arabic-text-screenshot-mac.h1: How to write Arabic on a screenshot on a Mac
arabic-text-screenshot-mac.intro: Many image tools write Arabic left to right or break the letters apart. EasyShoot detects Arabic and Hebrew as you type and writes them right to left with correct letter shaping, in any font on your Mac.

steps.name: Capture or open the image
steps.text: Take a screenshot, or copy an image and choose Open from Clipboard.

steps.name: Choose Text
steps.text: Press T and click where the text should go.

steps.name: Type in Arabic
steps.text: Type normally. With Direction set to Auto, EasyShoot switches to right to left by itself.

steps.name: Pick a font and size
steps.text: In the Style tab, choose any font on your Mac and set the Size. For a label that stands out, set Look to Background, Framed or Dark.

sections.html: Auto detects Arabic and Hebrew and writes right to left. Choose LTR or RTL to force a direction, for example for a line that mixes Arabic with English product names.
EasyShoot itself is available in Arabic, English, French, Spanish and German, and its windows follow the language's direction.

faq.q: Why do Arabic letters look separated in some apps?
faq.a: Arabic letters change shape depending on their neighbours. Apps that don't shape text draw each letter on its own; EasyShoot shapes text correctly.

faq.q: Can I mix Arabic and English in one note?
faq.a: Yes. Set the direction for the line, and numbers and Latin words stay in the right order.

faq.q: Does it support Hebrew?
faq.a: Yes. Auto direction detects Hebrew as well as Arabic.

take-screenshot-mac.title: How to take a screenshot on a Mac: every shortcut | EasyShoot
take-screenshot-mac.description: Every way to take a screenshot on a Mac: the whole screen, part of it or one window, straight to the clipboard, and where the files go.
take-screenshot-mac.h1: How to take a screenshot on a Mac
take-screenshot-mac.intro: Every Mac has screenshot shortcuts built in: Shift-Command-3, 4 and 5. Here is what each one does, how to copy a screenshot instead of saving it, and where the files go. If you want to mark up what you capture, EasyShoot adds its own shortcuts beside them.

steps.name: Capture the whole screen
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-3.

steps.name: Capture part of the screen
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-4 and drag over the area. Hold Space while you drag to move it, or press Esc to cancel.

steps.name: Capture a window
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-4, then Space. The pointer turns into a camera; click the window.

steps.name: Find or copy it
steps.text: The screenshot is saved to your desktop as a PNG file. To copy it instead, add Control, for example Control-Shift-Command-4.

steps.name: Mark it up, if you need to
steps.text: With EasyShoot, press Option-Shift-Command-4 instead, then click the thumbnail to add boxes, numbered steps, arrows or blur.

sections.html:
What you captureShortcut
The whole screenShift-Command-3
Part of the screenShift-Command-4, then drag
A window or a menuShift-Command-4, then Space
The Screenshot app, with a timer and optionsShift-Command-5
Copy instead of saveAdd Control to any of these

To leave a window's shadow out, hold Option while you click the window.

Press Shift-Command-5, click Options and pick a folder under Save to. The same menu sets a timer, shows the mouse pointer and turns the floating thumbnail on or off. To change the shortcuts themselves, open System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts › Screenshots.

sections.h2: Capture and mark up with EasyShoot
sections.html:
EasyShoot's shortcuts add Option to the Mac's own, so both sets keep working:

What you captureShortcut
Part of the screenOption-Shift-Command-4
A windowOption-Shift-Command-5
The whole screenOption-Shift-Command-3
An image you copiedOption-Shift-Command-7

By default, each capture is copied to the clipboard and shown as a thumbnail in the corner of the screen. Drag it into another app, save it, or click it to open the editor. Settings › General › After capture decides what happens on its own.

For a quick capture you keep or send as it is, the Mac's shortcuts are enough. EasyShoot helps when the screenshot has to explain or hide something: see how to add arrows and numbered steps, blur private details or crop a screenshot.

faq.q: Where do screenshots go on a Mac?
faq.a: To the desktop by default, as PNG files whose names start with Screenshot and include the date and time. Choose another folder in Shift-Command-5 › Options › Save to.

faq.q: How do I copy a screenshot to the clipboard on a Mac?
faq.a: Hold Control as well, for example Control-Shift-Command-4, then paste it anywhere. EasyShoot copies every capture to the clipboard by default; change that in its Settings › General.

faq.q: Can I change the screenshot shortcuts?
faq.a: Yes. The Mac's are in System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts › Screenshots, and EasyShoot's are in its Settings › Shortcuts.

faq.q: Why can't I capture some windows?
faq.a: Some apps, such as the Apple TV app, don't allow screenshots of their windows.

crop-screenshot-mac.title: How to crop a screenshot on a Mac | EasyShoot
crop-screenshot-mac.description: Crop a screenshot on your Mac with Markup or Preview, or in EasyShoot with ratios like 1:1 and 16:9 and an exact width for the exported image.
crop-screenshot-mac.h1: How to crop a screenshot on a Mac
crop-screenshot-mac.intro: The neatest crop is the one you never need: capture just the part you want. When you already have a screenshot, crop it in the Mac's Markup or Preview, or in EasyShoot with fixed ratios and an exact size.

steps.name: Open the screenshot
steps.text: Capture with Option-Shift-Command-4 and click the thumbnail, or open one you already have with Open Image… in the EasyShoot menu.

steps.name: Press C
steps.text: A frame appears around the picture, and the crop bar appears under the toolbar.

steps.name: Drag the frame
steps.text: Drag its edges or corners in to the part you want to keep. For a fixed shape, pick 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:10, 16:9 or 9:16 in the crop bar.

steps.name: Apply
steps.text: Press Return or click Apply. You can press C again later to change it.

steps.name: Set the size and share
steps.text: In the Export tab, resize by percent or to an exact width. Then press Shift-Command-C to copy or Command-S to save.

sections.h2: Crop with the Mac's own tools
sections.html:
• Right after a screenshot: click the thumbnail in the corner of the screen, click the Crop button in Markup and drag the corners.
  • In Preview: open the image, show the Markup toolbar, select the part to keep and click Crop.

Both are fine for a quick trim.
Option-Shift-Command-4 captures only the area you drag over, and Option-Shift-Command-5 captures one window without the rest of the screen. Either one often saves you the crop.

Crop decides which part of the picture you keep. Resize, in the Export tab, decides how many pixels the exported image has. With a background on, the aspect ratio in the toolbar sets the shape of the whole image; see how to add a background to a screenshot.

faq.q: How do I crop a screenshot to a square?
faq.a: Press C, choose 1:1 in the crop bar, move the frame where you want it and press Return.

faq.q: Can I undo a crop?
faq.a: Yes. Press Command-Z, or press C again and click Reset to bring back the whole picture.

faq.q: Does cropping lower the quality?
faq.a: No. The part you keep stays at full resolution. Only Resize in the Export tab changes the pixel size.

screenshot-background-mac.title: How to add a background to a screenshot on Mac | EasyShoot
screenshot-background-mac.description: Put a screenshot on a wallpaper, a gradient or a colour, with padding, rounded corners and a shadow, ready to post. A guide for Mac with EasyShoot.
screenshot-background-mac.h1: How to add a background to a screenshot on a Mac
screenshot-background-mac.intro: A screenshot with some space around it, rounded corners and a soft shadow looks ready for a post, a slide or a README. EasyShoot does this in its Background tab, and can keep the look for every screenshot after.

steps.name: Capture a window or an area
steps.text: Press Option-Shift-Command-5 and click a window, or Option-Shift-Command-4 and drag. Click the thumbnail to open the editor.

steps.name: Turn on the background
steps.text: In the Background tab, turn on Show background.

steps.name: Choose what goes behind
steps.text: Pick a wallpaper (your Mac's own, or EasyShoot's Waves and Gradients), a gradient or a single colour. Blur a wallpaper so the screenshot stays in front.

steps.name: Set padding, corners and shadow
steps.text: Move the Padding, Rounded corners and Shadow sliders until it looks right. Reset puts a slider back.

steps.name: Choose a shape
steps.text: Pick an aspect ratio in the toolbar, such as 1:1 for a square post or 16:9 for a slide.

steps.name: Copy or save
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-C to copy, or Command-S to save.

sections.h2: Aspect ratios for where you post
sections.html:
The aspect ratio menu sits in the toolbar beside Crop, and works while the background is on.

  • Auto: the padding wraps evenly around the screenshot.
  • 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:10, 16:9 and 9:16: the background grows so the whole image has that shape, and Alignment decides where the screenshot sits in it.
Open Presets in the editor's toolbar and choose Save Current Style as Preset…. In Settings › Presets, Make Default starts every new screenshot with it. You'll also find 12 starter looks there to add.
A window capture brings the window's own shadow. To use only the background's shadow, turn off Include window shadow in Settings › General; see how to screenshot a window without the shadow.

faq.q: Is there a free screenshot beautifier for Mac?
faq.a: EasyShoot is free. Its Background tab puts a screenshot on a wallpaper, a gradient or a colour, with padding, rounded corners and a shadow, and nothing is uploaded.

faq.q: Can I use my own picture as the background?
faq.a: No. You can pick one of your Mac's wallpapers, EasyShoot's Waves and Gradients, a gradient or a single colour.

faq.q: Does the background make the image bigger?
faq.a: Yes. Padding and the aspect ratio add space around the screenshot. To post at an exact size, set the width in the Export tab.

add-text-to-image-mac.title: How to add text to a picture on a Mac | EasyShoot
add-text-to-image-mac.description: Add a caption, a label or a note to any photo or image on your Mac, in any font, on a box that keeps it readable. Arabic and Hebrew work too.
add-text-to-image-mac.h1: How to add text to a picture on a Mac
add-text-to-image-mac.intro: EasyShoot isn't only for screenshots. Open any picture on your Mac, or one you've copied, and add a caption, a label or a note in any font. The file you opened stays as it was.

steps.name: Open the picture
steps.text: Click the EasyShoot icon in the menu bar, choose Open Image… and pick a photo or any other image. For a picture you've copied, press Option-Shift-Command-7.

steps.name: Choose Text
steps.text: Press T, click where the text should go and type.

steps.name: Pick a font and size
steps.text: In the Style tab, choose any font on your Mac or a Google font, and set the Size. You can also drag the text's corner.

steps.name: Make it stand out
steps.text: On a busy photo, set Look to Filled, Soft or Dark to put the text on a box, or Outlined to draw an outline around the letters.

steps.name: Save or copy
steps.text: Press Command-S to save a new file, or Shift-Command-C to copy it. Pick PNG, JPEG, HEIC or TIFF in the Export tab.

sections.html:
• Text: just the letters, in the colour you pick.
  • Filled, Soft and Dark: the text sits on a box, with corners from sharp to round.
  • Framed: a frame around the text, with no fill.
  • Outlined: an outline around the letters.
  • Custom: your own colours for the box.
Text can use any font installed on your Mac. Pick a Google font and EasyShoot downloads it the moment you choose it; that download and the check for updates are the only times the app goes online.
With Direction set to Auto, Arabic and Hebrew are written right to left, with the letters joined correctly. More in how to write Arabic on a screenshot.
The same editor adds arrows, boxes and numbered steps, hides faces or names with Pixelate (B) and crops the picture (C).

faq.q: Does this change my original photo?
faq.a: No. Command-S saves a new file in your save folder, and Save As… lets you choose a name and a place. The picture you opened isn't changed.

faq.q: Can I open iPhone photos?
faq.a: Yes. EasyShoot opens the image files your Mac can read, including HEIC photos from an iPhone.

faq.q: Can I change the text after adding it?
faq.a: Yes. Text and every other mark stay editable until you export the image.

faq.q: Is it free?
faq.a: Yes. EasyShoot is free and needs no account.

screenshot-without-shadow-mac.title: Screenshot a window without its shadow on Mac | EasyShoot
screenshot-without-shadow-mac.description: Window screenshots on a Mac come with a shadow and wide transparent edges. Leave it out with one key, or turn it off for good in EasyShoot.
screenshot-without-shadow-mac.h1: How to screenshot a window without the shadow on a Mac
screenshot-without-shadow-mac.intro: When you capture a window on a Mac, the picture includes the window's shadow, which adds wide transparent edges around it. You can leave the shadow out each time with one key, or turn it off for good in EasyShoot.

steps.name: Start a window capture
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-4, then Space. The pointer turns into a camera.

steps.name: Hold Option and click
steps.text: Hold Option while you click the window. The screenshot ends at the window's edge.

steps.name: Or turn it off in EasyShoot
steps.text: Open EasyShoot's Settings › General and turn off Include window shadow.

steps.name: Capture the window
steps.text: Press Option-Shift-Command-5 and click the window. Every window capture now comes without the shadow.

sections.html: The shadow is drawn on transparent pixels around the window. Pasted into a document, a chat or a slide, it can look like an uneven margin, and it makes the image larger than the window itself.
Turn the window shadow off, then use the Background tab to add padding, a background and a shadow as soft or strong as you like. See how to add a background to a screenshot.

faq.q: Why do my window screenshots have a shadow?
faq.a: macOS includes the window's shadow in window captures, on a transparent background, unless you hold Option while you click.

faq.q: Does the EasyShoot setting change the Mac's own shortcuts?
faq.a: No. It only changes window captures you take with EasyShoot. For Shift-Command-4 and Space, hold Option.

faq.q: Does it change area and full-screen captures?
faq.a: No. Those capture the screen as it looks; the setting only applies when you capture a window.

screenshot-pdf-page-mac.title: How to screenshot a PDF page and mark it up on Mac | EasyShoot
screenshot-pdf-page-mac.description: Share one page or part of a PDF as an image on your Mac, with arrows, numbered steps and blurred details, and when Preview is the better tool.
screenshot-pdf-page-mac.h1: How to screenshot a PDF page and mark it up on a Mac
screenshot-pdf-page-mac.intro: Sometimes you don't want to send the whole PDF, just one table or paragraph with an arrow pointing at it. Capture that part as an image, mark it up and paste it where people will see it. To edit the PDF itself, Preview is the better tool.

steps.name: Open the PDF and zoom in
steps.text: Open it in Preview or your browser and zoom in until the text is sharp. The capture is as sharp as what's on screen.

steps.name: Capture the part you need
steps.text: Press Option-Shift-Command-4 and drag over the page, the table or the paragraph. Click the thumbnail to open the editor.

steps.name: Mark it up
steps.text: Press R to box a line, N to number the steps, A for an arrow, or B to blur a name, an address or a signature.

steps.name: Share the image
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-C and paste it into a chat, an email or a document, or press Command-S to save it.

sections.h2: When Preview is the better tool
sections.html: EasyShoot opens images, not PDF files, and what it exports is a picture. To add notes, highlights or a signature to the PDF itself, or to redact text and keep a PDF, use the Markup toolbar in Preview.

Invoices, contracts and statements carry names, addresses and account numbers. Press B and drag over them before you share; the exported image keeps only the hidden version. More in how to blur part of a screenshot.
A PDF page holds a lot. Box the line that matters, number the fields to fill in, and crop the rest away with C so people see only what you mean.

faq.q: Can EasyShoot open a PDF file?
faq.a: No. It opens image files and images you've copied. Capture the PDF from the screen instead.

faq.q: How do I keep the text sharp?
faq.a: Zoom in on the PDF before you capture it. A screenshot keeps what's on your screen, so larger text on screen means sharper text in the image.

faq.q: Can I blur part of a PDF?
faq.a: On a capture, yes: press B and drag over it. To remove text from the PDF file itself, use the redaction tool in Preview.

cleanshot-x-alternative.title: CleanShot X alternative for Mac: EasyShoot compared | EasyShoot
cleanshot-x-alternative.description: Comparing EasyShoot and CleanShot X: capture, markup, privacy and price, with honest notes on when CleanShot X is the better choice.
cleanshot-x-alternative.h1: EasyShoot as a CleanShot X alternative
cleanshot-x-alternative.intro: CleanShot X is a popular, full-featured Mac capture app with screen recording and a cloud service. EasyShoot is a focused, free screenshot app that keeps everything on your Mac. Here is how they compare.
table: $35 one-time with one year of updates ($19/year to renew); Pro cloud plan $10 per user per month, billed yearly
Not listed on the pages read
Outline steps and other tools listed
Not needed for the app; used for Cloud

sections.html:
• You want screenshots only, with fast markup on single keys.
  • Nothing should leave your Mac: no account and no cloud.
  • You write Arabic or Hebrew on screenshots, or want the app in Arabic.
  • You'd rather not pay for a screenshot tool.

• You also record your screen or make GIFs.
  • You need text recognition (OCR).
  • Your team shares captures by link through a cloud service.

faq.q: Is EasyShoot a free alternative to CleanShot X?
faq.a: EasyShoot is free and covers capture, markup with shapes, arrows, text and numbered steps, pixelation, blur and backgrounds. It doesn't record video, capture scrolling pages or recognise text.

faq.q: Can I use both?
faq.a: Yes. Each app lets you set its own shortcuts, so you can give them different keys.

faq.q: Does EasyShoot upload screenshots?
faq.a: No. It has no account and no cloud; screenshots stay on your Mac.

shottr-alternative.title: Shottr alternative for Mac: EasyShoot compared | EasyShoot
shottr-alternative.description: Comparing EasyShoot and Shottr for Mac screenshots: capture, markup, privacy, languages and price, with notes on when Shottr fits better.
shottr-alternative.intro: Shottr is a small, fast Mac screenshot tool with OCR and many markup options. EasyShoot is a free, native app with no account, no uploads and full Arabic support. Here is how they compare.
table: Free to use; $12 or $30 one-time licences; licence required for commercial use

sections.html:
• You use the Mac in Arabic, French, Spanish or German, or write right to left on screenshots.
  • You want it free for work too, with nothing to license.
  • You prefer an app that never goes online with your screenshots.

• You need OCR or QR code reading.
  • You're on a Mac older than macOS 14.
  • You upload captures to your own S3 storage.

faq.q: Is EasyShoot free for commercial use?
faq.a: Yes. EasyShoot is free, with no licence to buy for work.

faq.q: Do both apps have scrolling capture?
faq.a: No. Shottr can capture long pages and chats as one image; EasyShoot captures an area, a window or the full screen.

faq.q: Which one supports Arabic?
faq.a: EasyShoot writes Arabic and Hebrew right to left with correct shaping and is available in Arabic. Shottr's pages don't mention Arabic.

snagit-alternative.title: Snagit alternative for Mac: EasyShoot compared | EasyShoot
snagit-alternative.description: Comparing EasyShoot and Snagit on Mac: capture, markup, privacy and price, with honest notes on when Snagit is the better pick.
snagit-alternative.h1: EasyShoot as a Snagit alternative on Mac
snagit-alternative.intro: Snagit by TechSmith is a long-running capture tool for Mac and Windows, sold as a yearly subscription with screen recording and sharing. EasyShoot is a free, Mac-only screenshot app with no account. Here is how they compare.
table: Copy, save or drag into any app

sections.html:
• You only need screenshots on a Mac and don't want a subscription.
  • You don't want to sign in to use a screenshot tool.
  • You want a background tool to make screenshots ready to post.

• You also work on Windows.
  • You record your screen with your voice and webcam.
  • Your team shares through TechSmith Screencast.

faq.q: Is there a free Snagit alternative for Mac?
faq.a: EasyShoot is free on Mac and covers capture, markup with shapes, arrows, text and numbered steps, pixelation, blur and backgrounds. It doesn't record video or capture scrolling pages.

faq.q: Does EasyShoot need an account?
faq.a: No. Open it and start; nothing to sign in to.

faq.q: Does EasyShoot run on Windows?
faq.a: No, EasyShoot is made for macOS only.

macos-screenshot-alternative.title: Better than Command-Shift-5? EasyShoot vs the Mac's tool
macos-screenshot-alternative.description: What EasyShoot adds to the screenshot tool built into macOS: numbered steps, pixelation and blur, shapes you can style, backgrounds and presets.
macos-screenshot-alternative.h1: EasyShoot vs the Mac's built-in Screenshot tool
macos-screenshot-alternative.intro: macOS includes a solid Screenshot tool (Shift-Command-5) with screen recording and Markup. EasyShoot builds on the same idea for screenshots you want to explain and share.
table: Shapes and text; numbered steps not listed
Not listed in Apple's Markup guide

sections.h2: When the built-in tool is enough
sections.html: For a quick capture, or a screen recording, Shift-Command-3, -4 and -5 do the job and are already on your Mac.

• Explaining something with numbered steps and arrows.
  • Hiding private details before you share.
  • Making screenshots ready to post with a background.
  • Giving a series of screenshots the same look with a saved preset.

faq.q: Can I keep using Shift-Command-4?
faq.a: Yes. EasyShoot uses Option-Shift-Command shortcuts by default, so the built-in ones keep working. You can change either set.

faq.q: Does EasyShoot replace Markup?
faq.a: For screenshots, yes: it adds numbered steps, pixelation and backgrounds on top of arrows, shapes and text.

faq.q: Is EasyShoot free?
faq.a: Yes.

lightshot-alternative.title: Lightshot alternative for Mac: EasyShoot compared | EasyShoot
lightshot-alternative.description: Comparing EasyShoot and Lightshot (prnt.sc) on Mac: capture, markup and privacy, including what happens to uploaded screenshots.
lightshot-alternative.h1: EasyShoot as a Lightshot alternative on Mac
lightshot-alternative.intro: Lightshot is a free, quick screenshot tool for Windows and Mac that can upload a capture to prnt.sc and give you a short link. EasyShoot is a free Mac app that keeps every screenshot on your Mac. Here is how they compare.
table: Windows, Mac (macOS 10.7 or later) and browser extensions
Copy, save or drag into any app
Optional upload to prnt.sc with a short link
Only people you send them to
Lightshot's privacy policy says uploaded images are public and reachable by URL

sections.html:
• Your screenshots show private things and shouldn't be on a public server.
  • You want numbered steps, pixelation and a background tool.
  • You need window or fullscreen capture on a Mac.

• You work on Windows, or want a browser extension.
  • You want a public short link to paste anywhere, and the image isn't private.
  • You use its search for similar images.
Lightshot's privacy policy says every uploaded image is public and has its own URL. Uploading is optional: if you only save or copy, nothing is uploaded. EasyShoot has no upload at all.

faq.q: Is there a private alternative to Lightshot on Mac?
faq.a: EasyShoot keeps screenshots on your Mac: no account, no cloud and no upload. You share by copying, saving or dragging.

faq.q: Are Lightshot uploads public?
faq.a: Lightshot's privacy policy says uploaded images are public and reachable by their URL. Saving or copying without uploading keeps them local.

faq.q: Can I keep Lightshot's shortcut?
faq.a: Lightshot's Mac download page lists Shift-Command-9. EasyShoot uses Option-Shift-Command shortcuts by default, and you can change them.
